continue to work on a libpldm based solution.

I've added all TOF members here because:

1. A new repository requires a TOF issue anyhow.
2. This seems like a "maintainer and contributor cannot come to consensus" problem, which the TOF should help address, especially if it has gone on for 8 months.

Overall, I'm not in support of this.

I'd much rather see us go to a pattern similar to libgpio, where the C++ bindings and C bindings are both available in the same repository and the package publishes two libraries, two sets of examples, and has a largely 1:1 abstraction where everything is implemented in portable C, and C++ RAII classes are made available through gpiocxx to implement common safety operations.

Overall, I defer most of my own judgement to Andrew, who has more knowledge of PLDM and has maintained the library.


At a much higher level, we need to understand why the abstractions of one protocol (PLDM) leaked into the greater system.  To some extent that's because the "PLDM package" type really isn't about PLDM as a protocol;  It's a file format that just happens to be governed by the same spec, and gets used in other contexts (redfish, ssh, etc).  Given that, a design where pldmd itself wasn't in charge of the pldm file format would remove the need for shared code entirely keeping the "unpack a pldm package" logic in one repository.  Accomplishing that would be difficult and error prone, so people duplicated the code.
Can you give a pointer to where these are?
Done
This shouldn't be used as justification for a separate library.

If the time it takes to get something into libpldm exceeds the effort needed to maintain it separately, the time-based argument makes sense to me.


At that point it might make sense to maintain it separately.
Of course there are other tradeoffs, discussed in this design.
Are you actually proposing ABI stability or just API stability?  Those are different problems.  ABI stability in C++ is rather hard as even libstdc++ changes can result in ABI in-stability.

I'm assuming he actually means ABI given he checked in an ABI file into the repo.

Alexander, lets just remove this section, as it distracts from the goal you're trying to accomplish.  If we want to argue that libX libraries need to maintain ABI compatibility, that's probably something to be argued and engineered separately from "we need a new API".

> Alexander, lets just remove this section

Done

With respect, this isn't a design.  Which interfaces are exposed from this library?  How does this library interact with libpldm?  What code should be checked in here, and what code should be checked into libpldm?

> Which interfaces are exposed from this library?

design template https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/b7c51760000b867314376a3ac6570ac8b9f97353/designs/design-template.md?plain=1#L91

says to not include code here.

> What code should be checked in here

C++ code. libpldm is a C library.

> and what code should be checked into libpldm?

The C code.
nit, remove "continue trying to".  Also add more details about how the abstraction will work.

> nit, remove "continue trying to"

Done.

> Also add more details about how the abstraction will work.

The abstraction is already implemented. Refer to the `PackageParser` implementation which has been linked. What's left is just some API details which are not to be discussed in design review (as per design template).
This is a strange rationale... isn't it?  "My quality isn't good enough for one maintainer so I want my own sandbox where I don't have to have the same level of quality".
+1.  "Nothing has merged" isn't a technical argument.  We need to make the technical argument that this code is quality enough for shared use.

> We need to make the technical argument that this code is quality enough for shared use.

You are aware that PackageParser has been merged into 2 separate OpenBMC repositories already.

Is it not sufficient a technical argument to deduplicate some piece of code?

Technically it's already a shared code due to the duplication.

It's not like the code itself gets any worse from being in a separate repo.
Have the authors/maintainers of the duplicated code reviewed the new code you're proposing?  I don't see them on the review?

I don't see how i can fix this issue. Can't force people to review the code.
Closing this comment.

With respect, the status quo of implementing a feature in portable C is what the project has decided in the past.   I'm happy to field and welcome challenging assumptions, but if your goal is timeframe, following the status quo, helping others to do the same is the likely the fastest approach.

If your goal is to build something new, and challenge assumptions (which this doc seems to do a great job of) then you need to expect that things will move slower as consensus is reached.

> With respect, the status quo of implementing a feature in portable C is what the project has decided in the past

I don't get this sentence. The proposed implementation is in C++. Always has been.

> then you need to expect that things will move slower as consensus is reached.

Taking an existing code (which has been reviewed twice, in 2 different repositories) to be de-duplicated looks like a straightforward effort to me.

Let's see how long this project takes to reach consensus on if that's okay.
Remove.  Lets keep this doc on technical aspects, not personal.
Done
Please make a more technical argument here.

It's a dependency argument.

Projects usually don't like taking transitive dependencies which are unnecessary.

And projects don't like taking dependencies on other projects which have runtime components.

Leaf projects (applications) usually take dependencies on libraries.
Lets just remove this.  "security issues" are about more than just pointers, and I don't think this section adequately handles that.
Right. It's a filler sentence, without any content. Removed.

A request for a new repository would need an accompanying TOF issue to request the repository.  From a discussion within the TOF, it doesn't seem like the libpldm maintainer is currently being unreasonable and it seems like progress is being made.  Please continue to work the libpldm side.

If you think the libpldm maintainer is being unreasonable, let's create a TOF issue to discuss those specific issues.  I would suggest you have concrete actions that you'd like the project to take in order to make progress (ie. what is the maintainer not accepting that you think is unreasonable and we should document a overriding decision).
